The main report separates copied worktrees, archives and older project variants.
Each entry gives the original location, literal count and saved surrounding text.
These excerpts do not establish who authored the words.

### .claude/skills/.archive/metaform-spec-amendments/SKILL.md

Source: [line 15](/home/rich/metaform/.claude/skills/.archive/metaform-spec-amendments/SKILL.md:15). Literal uses: 1.

~~~text
13: - Mirror the existing amendments in `specifications/01-map.md` and `specifications/04-chassis-modules.md`; grep those files for `- Amendment,` to match the form before writing one.
14: - Do not edit the code to match a spec; the code is the reference, and the spec follows it.
15: - Before a record's Status or Build says "built", find the switch that gates the built code and read its value. grep for the constant that turns the feature off. On 2026-10-15 `LINK_LOCK = False` in `runner.py` left CTX-060 to CTX-064 described as in force while none of them held. Run the record's acceptance tests with `-rs`; a skipped test is not shown, and the record says so instead of Status "built".
16: - When a ticket's code makes a sentence of a record false, a worker does not leave it as a note alone. It drafts the bullet into `artifacts/specs-draft/` in the same run, names that file in its final resolution, and says which sentence the code now contradicts.
17: - Check the record's earlier amendments as well as its original sentences: an amendment from a prior ticket can be what the new code contradicts. Then the draft is a superseding bullet that names that amendment by date and ticket and quotes the sentence it replaces. Never rewrite the earlier bullet in place.
~~~

Source: [line 329](/home/rich/metaform/.claude/skills/metaform-development/SKILL.md:329). Literal uses: 1.

~~~text
327: ## Spec records: amend by a dated bullet, never rewrite
328: - When code changes what a `specifications/*.md` record says, leave the original sentences and append one bullet after the record's `Status:` line, inside the same record: `- Amendment, YYYY-MM-DD, ticket <id>, <what changed and why>.` Use the date of the change, not the record's first date. Mirror the `- Amendment,` bullets in `specifications/01-map.md` and `specifications/04-chassis-modules.md`. Never create a new record number for an amendment.
329: - Before a record says "built", find the constant that gates the built code (for example `LINK_LOCK = False` in `runner.py`) and run the record's acceptance tests with `-rs`. A skipped test is not built.
330: - An agent never edits `specifications/` directly, even when its ticket asks. It drafts the wording into `artifacts/specs-draft/` (link the file first with `dispatch_link file=... node=<Address>`), names that file in the resolution, and the bullet lands only after the owner approves that exact wording, marked `approved by the owner`.
331: - Check the record's earlier amendments as well as its original sentences. When a new amendment supersedes one, quote the sentence it replaces and name the earlier bullet by date and ticket. Never rewrite the earlier bullet in place.
~~~

28: - Preserve authored prompts, source documents, aliases, fields, folder references, answers, and retained revisions. Do not turn development instructions into runtime prompts. Do not add speculative quality gates for agent answers.
29: - A submission must carry its issued nonce/header. PID identifies a process; it never establishes agent or assignment identity. Transport initialization metadata is not a substitute for the assignment contract.
30: - Initial storage is global. Configured project/global and split/unified placement remain physical choices; a join type does not intrinsically own a database. No automatic destructive migration of existing user data.

~~~text
29: - **What happens.**
30:   - The design depends on `disable-model-invocation: true` and `$ARGUMENTS`, and both are Claude Code-only.
31:   - Codex reads `$HOME/.agents/skills` as its USER scope. It gates implicit use only through `agents/openai.yaml` `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false`, and puts every skill's name, description and path in its first list.
32:   - Gemini CLI reads `~/.agents/skills` as an alias of `~/.gemini/skills`. It "injects the name and description of all enabled skills into the system prompt" and activates them by matching.
33:   - So every Codex and Gemini session on a machine where any tool was installed carries "Read one node of the Metaform map … through the metaform command line". That is a CLI route competing with `map_where`, which goes against MCP-021's 2026-10-06 MCP-first amendment.
~~~

81: ### F5 (major): `held=true`, the "release" control, holds nothing; autostart starts held Backlog tickets
82: - **What happens.** VIEW-045 says planned tickets go to Backlog held, "which they release". The sentinel and system agent are told to write `held=true`. But `start_work()` filters only the separate `hold` setting, so autostart starts held Backlog tickets after To do with no release at all. The person and the agent each believe the other one gates the start.
83: - **Evidence (observed).** `scratchpad/ux1orch-zq/heldstart.py`, with two tickets `held=true` (`map work hold=true` counts `"held":true` ×2), `dispatch_autostart` on and `run_reserved` replaced: both were reserved (`'planned by system agent'` ×2 in the reserved list). Code: `dispatch/__init__.py:1831-1834` (only `kept.hold` excluded; `record.held` is only a sort key at :1840).
84:   - Noun texts (`metaform help map work`): `held`: "keep it waiting until agents are assigned or take it"; `hold`: "hidden from agents and automatic starts until the person lets it go".
~~~

~~~text
103: - Requirement: A verb declared with a caution does nothing until called with `--confirm`, and without it prints the caution and the exact confirming command.
104: - What this means: The caution text says what will be lost. The confirming command is the same command plus `--confirm`.
105: - Why: The main agent that holds the confirming command acts with confidence; a subagent meeting only the caution hesitates. The wording steers, and nothing gates inference.
106: - How it shows: `metaform hello forget` prints the caution and `Next: If you are sure: metaform hello forget --confirm`.
107: - Build: `Verb.caution`, BASE-035, checked by the dispatcher as in CLI-018 and by the MCP module as in MCP-006.
~~~

154: - Profile application allocation, draw calls, frame-time median/p95/p99, simulation-step time, queue depth, and patch latency. Record hardware and fixture sizes. Performance targets require measured reference hardware before becoming acceptance thresholds.
155: 
156: Capacity recommendation for the first benchmark fixture: two browser clients, one agent, two regions, four streamed chunks, 100 dynamic bodies, and one extension. This fixture is a test scope, not a production capacity promise. Increase load only after correctness gates pass.
157: 
158: Architecture must settle storage transactions, hard sandbox enforcement, canonical schemas, border transfer details, durable receipt projection, and protocol compatibility. These are engineering decisions supported by this brief. Product decisions about public hosting, billing, marketplaces, and mass concurrency remain outside this preparation's requested core.
~~~

342: - **M5-SCHEMA-FIDELITY-1:** `evaluate.pin_fidelity` declares `tempo.fidelity-report.v1`, but that schema was absent from the shipped bundle. The build added a strict candidate/pin coverage contract with evidence, tolerance, preserved/violated status, departure location, aggregate preservation, and an unverified ledger. Proposed verdict: ratify or replace with an author-supplied contract.
343: - **M5-SCHEMA-EVALUATION-1:** the shipped evaluation schema made `removal_tripwire_fired` optional and had no contract for mandatory full re-verification or repair/reinvent goal checks. The build made the tripwire required and added explicit full-reverification evidence, repair minimality, reinvent novelty, and the seven §7.1 viability gates. Proposed verdict: ratify this narrow completion of the operation-declared output schema.
344: - **M5-SCHEMA-VERDICT-1:** the shipped verdict schema did not require clause-by-clause results or the insufficient-evidence ledger named by the prompt. The build made both required so the deterministic shell can verify promotion mechanically. Proposed verdict: ratify this completion.
345: - **M5-MUTATION-ADAPTER-1:** mutation operations return artifact-native work rather than one universal JSON shape. The current model adapter requires a small schema-valid envelope containing the artifact, change note, removal declaration, touched pins, and unverified ledger; the artifact itself remains unconstrained JSON data. Proposed verdict: retain this transport envelope or supply a different universal adapter contract.
~~~
